plain_english: Free of every thought, pure, at peace, beyond rising and dissolving — in that supreme principle shines the world, thirty-six in nature.
sanskrit_cite: sarvavikalpavihīnaṃ śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ layodayavihīnam | yat paratattvaṃ tasmin vibhāti ṣaṭṭriṃśadātma jagat

plain_english: As towns and villages, varied yet undivided in a mirror's orb, shine out in division, each from each and from the mirror too.
sanskrit_cite: darpaṇabimbe yadvan nagaragrāmādicitram avibhāgi | bhāti vibhāgenaiva ca parasparaṃ darpaṇād api ca

plain_english: From the purest knowing of supreme Bhairava: though void of division, the world shines forth divided, each from each and thence.
sanskrit_cite: vimalatamaparamabhairavabodhāt tadvad vibhāgaśūnyam api | anyonyaṃ ca tato 'pi ca vibhaktam ābhāti jagad etat

plain_english: Śiva, power, Sadāśiva, then the Īśvara-Vidyā-formed principle-state — the five powers, in divided nature, He lights up.
sanskrit_cite: śivaśaktisadāśivatām īśvaravidyāmayīṃ ca tattvadaśām | śaktīnāṃ pañcānāṃ vibhaktabhāvena bhāsayati

plain_english: Supreme is the freedom that effects the hard thing, the great Lord's own; the goddess, Māyā-power, veils Śiva's self — that is it.
sanskrit_cite: paramaṃ yat svātantryaṃ durghaṭasaṃpādanaṃ maheśasya | devī māyāśaktiḥ svātmāvaraṇaṃ śivasya itat

plain_english: Grasped by Māyā, knowing turns stained and the person becomes a bound beast, fettered by time, art, limit, passion, ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: māyāparigrahavaśād bodho malinaḥ pumān paśur bhavati | kālakalāniyatibalād rāgāvidyāvaśena saṃbaddhaḥ

plain_english: Here and now I know but little, with my whole self: six sheaths with Māyā are the atom's inner limbs, so it is said.
sanskrit_cite: adhunaiva kiṃcid evedam eva sarvātmanaiva jānāmi | māyāsahitaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam aṇor antaraṅgam idam uktam

plain_english: Like husk settled on rice-grain, separate yet undivided, purity comes by turning to Śiva's path with longing.
sanskrit_cite: kambukam iva ta.ṅdulakaṇaviniviṣṭaṃ bhinnam apy abhidā | bhajate tat tu viśuddhiṃ śivamārgaunmukhyayogena

plain_english: Mere pleasure, pain, delusion — from resolve, will, and I-sense; then nature, then the inner organ: intellect, mind, ego in turn.
sanskrit_cite: sukhaduḥkhamohamātraṃ niścayasaṃkalpanābhimānāc ca | prakṛtir athāntaḥkaranaṃ buddhimano'haṃkṛtikramaśaḥ
